scope: Theorem 1.1 (Interfaces and all nested loops) of the manuscript “Conformal Limits of Critical Square-Lattice Random-Cluster Interfaces” (preprints/Conformal-Limits-of-Critical-Square-Lattice-Random-Cluster-Interfaces-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b14b09c2088272ae), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed real 1 ≤ q ≤ 4, the following assertions hold. (i) For every bounded Jordan domain D with distinct boundary marks a, b, and every approximation satisfying (1.3), the Dobrushin strand ηn converges in law, in (1.4), to chordal SLEκ(q) from a to b in D. (ii) Under the specified free infinite-volume law, Γδ converges in law as δ ↓ 0 to the nested whole-plane CLEκ(q), in the spherical collection topology just defined. The limit is Möbius invariant. Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence. No uniformity in q is asserted.
